source.title: REVS: Unlearning Sensitive Information in Language Models via Rank Editing in the Vocabulary Space
source.authors: Tomer Ashuach; Martin Tutek; Yonatan Belinkov

page_placements.theme: Internal analyses: changes concentrated late or along a direction, target representations stay close to the original

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning effectiveness and resistance to its own white-box extraction attacks using PII token-rank metrics. This bears on whether unlearning leaves information recoverable, but it does not use the specific recovery tests named in most claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper tests unlearning methods and extraction attacks on sensitive PII, not broad conceptual knowledge. Its attacks are Logit-Lens, Delta, and a white-box Perturbation Attack; the latter inserts spaces into prompts and probes internal representations. It does not report fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting-only recovery. The reported Efficacy@100 and Resistance Score are rank-based measures, not targeted-knowledge accuracy against a never-trained model.
record.test_reason: The study proposes REVS, an unlearning method for memorized PII in Llama-3-8B and GPT-J-6B. It measures rank-based forgetting, retain-set specificity, MMLU/GSM8K, and resistance to white-box residual-stream readout attacks (Logit-Lens, Delta, Perturbation) against six adapted baselines. These results bear on A (does unlearning work and resist simple attacks) and on F (a newer method claiming robustness). On synthetic SSNs, efficacy on unseen prompts for the same SSN (Generalization@100, Table 1/3) bears on E (rephrasing). There is no fine-tuning, direction-ablation or quantization attack. Targets are token sequences (PII), not conceptual knowledge.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct: REVS beats six baselines on unlearning score and is best or second-best on resistance, with stable MMLU/GSM8K except a GSM8K drop on SSN. The authors also note higher efficacy goes with higher resistance, and an efficacy–specificity trade-off. Their Limitations section asks for more fine-grained and probe-based attacks.
record.recipe_differences: REVS is a newly proposed non-gradient rank-editing method that modifies selected MLP neurons in vocabulary space; the study also evaluates adapted implementations of several existing unlearning baselines. It does not reproduce the original methods named in the claim as a recovery-attack study.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model change efficacy, specificity, and extraction resistance. The paper reports that URL results use the Email hyperparameters, and that REVS resistance varies by PII dataset. For Llama-3-8B URLs, RMU and NPO-KL have lower Perturbation Attack scores than the unedited model.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama URLs, RMU and NPO-KL Perturb scores (13.88/13.50) fall below the unedited 36.00. Authors read this as internal memorization persisting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some unlearning methods make perturbed-prompt hidden-state readout of the target easier than before unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2024)
record.problems: The study's attack results are white-box rank-based extraction measures, not the specific fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attacks in the claim. It does not compare against a never-trained target model. Some Llama-3-8B settings show reduced specificity, and the paper notes a GSM8K drop for SSN. GPT-J-6B general-capability benchmarks were not evaluated because the unedited model was near random chance on MMLU.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, individual Logit-Lens, Delta, and Perturbation component scores for the remaining model-method-dataset combinations are omitted; Tables 2 and 4 report them. Additional REVS hyperparameter and neuron/token-selection ablations are in Figures 4 and 6 and Tables 7-9. The included aggregate Resistance Score combines the three attack measures.

untested.parts: Comparison with a never-trained model or chance level; conceptual-knowledge benchmarks (WMDP/TOFU); GPT-J capability benchmarks (skipped because the unedited model was near chance on MMLU).
All of it: no relearning by fine-tuning.
No direction ablation. Logit-lens readout is the only internal analysis, and it scores equal to output efficacy.
Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information. Only unseen same-target prompts on SSN were tested; the Perturbation attack reads hidden states.
Resistance of REVS to fine-tuning, ablation, quantization and black-box prompting attacks.

missing.what: Generalization@100 (efficacy on unseen prompts eliciting the same SSN) for all methods; needed for the E rephrasing verdict.
Baseline Efficacy@100, specificity and MMLU/GSM8K; needed for A on baselines.

record.verdict_notes: Logit Lens@100 equals Efficacy@100 in almost every Table 2/4 cell, so the Resistance Score is capped by output efficacy. It mostly shows whether unlearning worked at the output, not whether hidden information was recovered. Unedited Delta/Perturb scores are high (e.g. 96.80/92.13 on SSN), which makes those components weak attacks. The reader's F 'challenges' label used baseline rows and an MMLU row; it is dropped. Baselines were modified to target single tokens and tuned by the authors. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: It evaluates token-rank efficacy, specificity/general capabilities, and extraction resistance, but does not test near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy or compare against a model that never learned the target information.
No recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples is tested.
No activation-direction ablation is performed, and the paper does not establish that unlearning merely blocks access rather than deleting information.
No prompting-only rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context-information recovery is tested. The Perturbation Attack is white-box and uses internal representations.

REVS is evaluated against the paper's Logit-Lens, Delta, and white-box Perturbation attacks, not against fine-tuning recovery, direction ablation, quantization, or the prompting-only attacks listed in the claim.

source_check.notes: In Table 1 (Llama SSN) the column order is Unlearning, Efficacy, General., Specificity. General. is the 3rd block (REVS 89.67), Specificity the 4th (REVS 82.17); Table 3 and the A.3 text confirm this order. Efficacy, generalization and resistance are rank-based Score@100, not accuracy against chance. MMLU/GSM8K were not run on GPT-J. URL runs reuse the Email hyperparameters.

statements.correction: REVS models: Llama-3-8B and GPT-J-6B. Efficacy and resistance are rank-based Score@100, not accuracy against chance. Llama SSN: MMLU 61.05->60.87, GSM8K 47.83->44.20, specificity 82.17. GPT-J specificity: 70.33 (SSN), 68.98 (Emails). GPT-J Emails resistance: 83.48. MMLU/GSM8K not run on GPT-J (MMLU near chance, 26-27).
statements.problem: The REVS numbers are right, but the conditions say models are 7-70B, and REVS used GPT-J-6B and Llama-3-8B. The statement cites only MMLU, leaving out REVS's own costs in the same settings: the GSM8K drop on Llama SSN, specificity below 100, and incomplete resistance on GPT-J Emails.

statements.correction: REVS resistance on SSN: 99.27 (Llama-3-8B, Table 2) and 99.12 (GPT-J-6B, Table 4). Attacks: Logit-Lens, Delta, Perturbation.

Llama-3-8B REVS resistance: SSN 99.27, Emails 71.95, URLs 82.80. Efficacy on the same splits is also lower (Emails 59.65, URLs 78.22). URL runs reuse the Email hyperparameters. REVS is a close second to Max-Entropy (72.77) on Emails.
Section 4.5: hyperparameters were tuned on SSN and Emails, and URLs reuse the Email hyperparameters.
Table 2, Llama URLs, Perturb@100: RMU 13.88, NPO-KL 13.50, unedited 36.00. Appendix A.1 reads this as internal memorization persisting.
